entries.test: Authenticated Microsoft planning documents would show whether the planned transition covered all GitHub Copilot customers starting in June 2026.
entries.note: This concerns the documented plan, rather than whether rollout ultimately matched it.

entries.test: GitHub's published pricing and billing records for June through August 2026 would establish the subscription charges and pooled credit allowances.
entries.note: The proposition omits the explicit caveat that amounts may change before launch, although the extracted conditions retain it.

entries.test: GitHub's pricing and credit allowances following the June–August 2026 promotion would establish whether Business provided $19 in tokens for $19 and Enterprise $39 for $39.
entries.note: The proposition omits the caveat that amounts may change before launch. The amounts concern Business and Enterprise.
“Is expected” reports a qualified expectation rather than a firm personal prediction. The body separately gives April 23, conflicting with “next week.”

entries.test: Microsoft's billing announcements and disclosed AI compute expenditure would establish whether the transition coincided with sharply increasing compute costs.
entries.note: “As” places the transition in the context of rising costs without expressly claiming that those costs caused it.

entries.test: Microsoft's contemporaneous announcements and GitHub plan documentation would establish the signup suspensions, Opus removal, and announced plans to tighten usage limits.
entries.note: The final component reports an existing plan, rather than guaranteeing its implementation.

entries.test: Dated Microsoft announcements and GitHub rollout records would establish whether the announcement occurred April 23, 2026, and changes began rolling out at the beginning of June.
entries.note: The documents are the stated source for this forecast. Its announcement date conflicts with the executive summary.

entries.test: Authenticated planning documents and information available on April 22, 2026, would establish whether all users were covered while individual Pro and Pro+ arrangements remained unspecified.
entries.note: The uncertainty concerns information available when the post appeared, rather than whether individual arrangements were later clarified.
